documents.title: Dissertation & Thesis Handbook (Generative AI section)
documents.stance_why: The section says AI "can be used as a tool for supporting thinking, research, and writing" but "cannot be used to replace these acts", requires consulting the committee chair beforehand, and bans "AI-generated writing in their thesis or dissertation". AI is thus allowed only for narrow, chair-approved research uses, which is restrict rather than permit or delegates because a flat ban and disclosure duties are set by the document itself.
documents.summary: A short generative-AI section in the Graduate School thesis and dissertation handbook. AI may support research but not replace thinking or writing; students must consult their chair first, may not include AI-generated writing, must cite AI used in research, and violations count as academic dishonesty. It covers only graduate theses and dissertations.

units.why: The handbook opens its AI section by saying AI "blurs ethical boundaries, outstripping traditional policies and rules regarding plagiarism". This is a framing statement of why the section exists (informs, general, all). P56 fits as the institution-level preamble stating purpose and principles; P54 does not fit because no review is promised.
units.anchor: AI is a rapidly shifting new tool that blurs ethical boundaries

units.why: "AI can be used as a tool for supporting thinking, research, and writing" allows AI in thesis research and manuscript development, so it is a permission (may) for students. P62 fits because it governs AI in theses and manuscripts; P12 is for coursework tutoring.
units.anchor: AI can be used as a tool for supporting thinking, research, and writing

units.why: "AI cannot be used to replace these acts" bars AI from replacing thinking, research and writing, so students must remain the primary thinker. P32 fits better than P19 because the sentence is about replacing thinking, not about submitting generated text (that is the later sentence).
units.anchor: AI cannot be used to replace these acts

units.why: "they must consult with their committee chair beforehand" requires students to ask the chair before using generative AI in research, which is the ask-first rule (P10) rather than P04 because it is a duty on the student to seek approval.
units.anchor: they must consult with their committee chair beforehand

units.why: "They must adhere to guidance from their chair" hands the decision on acceptable AI use to the committee chair, an individual faculty member, so it is P04 (each instructor or chair sets the rule); it binds the student.
units.anchor: They must adhere to guidance from their chair

units.why: "graduate students cannot use AI-generated writing in their thesis or dissertation" is a flat ban on submitting AI-generated text as the manuscript, so P19 (do not have AI produce the work you submit) with must-not and prohibit.
units.anchor: graduate students cannot use AI-generated writing in their thesis or dissertation

units.why: "that use must be detailed and cited according to the academic publishing guidelines in their field" requires disclosure of AI used in the research process (searches, keywords, data analysis). P24 fits; P25 does not because no tool/prompt details are specified, and the citation style is deferred to field guidelines.
units.anchor: that use must be detailed and cited according to the academic publishing guidelines

units.why: "students must be able to clearly explain and replicate the process of using AI" requires students to be able to explain and reproduce their AI-assisted research process when asked. P30 fits (explain what is submitted); P62 does not add since this is an accountability duty.
units.anchor: students must be able to clearly explain and replicate the process of using AI

units.why: "Failure to adhere to this policy constitutes academic dishonesty" classifies violations of the AI rules as academic dishonesty, so P36 (unauthorized AI use as misconduct); no specific penalty is stated, so P37 does not fit.
units.anchor: Failure to adhere to this policy constitutes academic dishonesty

notes: Only one included document (graduate thesis handbook, one short AI section). No university-wide student AI policy, school, computing or course documents were collected. Text read in full; only the Ethical Conduct section concerns AI. The statement that plagiarism is a serious offense was not coded as it is not AI-specific.
